full_judgment:
2. Facts, in brief, are that the respondent No. 1, as plaintiff, filed the above suit seeking declaration of his title in the land as described Ka schedule of the plaint and also recovery of possession of the land described in schedule Kha of the plaint on the averments that .21 acres of land of Plot No. 243 described in Ka schedule belonged to Nayeb Ali who transferred the same to Rahim Sheikh by kabala dated 8.2.1939 and after the death of Rahim Sheikh his son Mahtab Sheikh became owner of the same and then Mahtab Sheikh, in 14th Chaitra 1346 settled the same in favour of Hemat Ali, the father of the plaintiff. Nayeb Ali by Patta dated 4.8.1938 and then Tezarat and Alekjan by Patta dated 8.2.1939 also settled Kha schedule land to Rahim Sheikh and after his death Mahtab became owner of the same and he by a registered kabuliyat dated 28.5.48 settled the same in favour of his son Hemat Ali who then gifted the .21 acres of land of Plot No. 243, that is Ka schedule, to the plaintiff and by kabala dated 23.1.1957 also transferred .17 acres of land of Plot No. 254 from Kha schedule land to the plaintiff and then on 15th Magh 1383 B.S, the plaintiff, for the first time, came to know that. 17 acre of land of Plot No. 254, that is Kha schedule land, has been wrongly recorded in the name of Rajab Ali and then he filed Title Suit No. 256 of 1973 against them and since they failed to appear the above suit was decreed exparte and that regarding .21 acres of land of Plot No. 243, which is Ka schedule land, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 69 of 1976 but in view of a compromise which was made to the effect that plaintiff will possess Ka schedule land and Rahela Khatoon, who installed the defendant/petitioner in the suit land as her bargadar, will possess Kha schedule land, the plaintiff, in good faith, withdrew the above suit but no deed of exchange was then executed to the above effect and on the other the defendant, on 25.3.1986, dispossessed the plaintiff from Kha schedule land by erecting a house therein; subsequently after series of shalish the defendant handed over the Ka schedule of land to the plaintiff wherein he is living with his family and that the defendants, having denied his title in the suit land, he had to file the suit. 

 3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material facts and contending that Rahim Sheikh, while owning and possessing both Ka and Kha schedule land, died leaving behind Mahatab Sheikh who, in the year 1346 B.S, orally settled the same in favour of Barkatullah, who then by Patta dated 16.7.1952 transferred his interest in the said land in favour of Yousuf Ali Biswas who in turn, by registered sale deed dated 19 Kartik 1362 B.S, transferred the same to Rajeb Ali Kazi and Maksed All Kazi who then by a registered deed of sale dated 3.10.73 transferred the same to Hasina Khatun and then Hasina Khatun by registered deed of sale dated 27.2.1976 transferred the same to Rahela Khatun who is possessing the same through defendant No.1, her bargadar and that Rahela Khatun by an agreement transfer schedules Ka and Kha land to the defendant No.1 and also one Latifur Rahman, her relation, but having not executed the sale deed the defendant No.1 and said Latifur Rahman filed a suit for specific performance of contract and obtained sale deed through court on 23.5.1990; subsequently the defendant No.1 after possessing the suit land from more than 12 years, in terms of an argument for sale and on accepting Tk.24,000.00, handed over possession of the same to Mujibur Rahman  and since then said Mujibur Rahman is possessing the suit land and Mujibur Rahman is a bonafide purchaser for value and that in the meantime a miscellaneous case has been filed praying for setting aside the decree obtained by the petitioner against Rahela Khatoon.
